title: Mesoscale eddy statistics and their thermohaline imprint
query: Using the supplied CMOMS daily velocity, temperature and salinity for 2011-2020, test the following findings of Chen et al. (2011, Journal of Geophysical Research, doi:10.1029/2010JC006716) on South China Sea mesoscale eddies: (1) eddies are generated mainly along a northeast-southwest band and southwest of the Luzon Strait, with similar numbers of anticyclonic and cyclonic eddies in most regions; (2) the mean eddy radius is about 132 km and the mean lifetime about 8.8 weeks; (3) in the northern South China Sea eddies propagate southwestward along the continental slope at about 5-9 cm/s, while in the central basin they move roughly westward at about 2-6 cm/s; (4) cyclonic eddies make the thermocline shallower, thinner and stronger, anticyclonic eddies make it deeper, thicker and weaker, and the halocline responds similarly; (5) eddy activity is sensitive to wind-stress curl and, in the northern South China Sea, to the strength of the background flow. The paper detected eddies in satellite altimetry; choose and justify a detection and tracking method for the model fields and state its parameters. Give a verdict for each finding (reproduced, partly reproduced, not reproduced, or not testable with the supplied data) with quantitative evidence, and explain differences from the paper.

paper.title: Mesoscale eddies in the South China Sea: Mean properties, spatiotemporal variability, and impact on thermohaline structure
